candidates.name: medellin-airbnb-displacement-risk
candidates.what_it_holds: Pipeline flagging Medellin/Barranquilla, Colombia neighborhoods where Airbnb growth concentrates in low-income areas. Committed: comuna_estrato.csv (Medellin socioeconomic strata by comuna), barranquilla_barrio_estrato.csv (parcel-level ESTRATO_1994 layer, maintained through 2025), dane_housing_blocks.geojson (DANE 2018 census block housing counts), medellin_barrio_housing.csv / barranquilla_barrio_housing.csv (aggregated housing units), plus geospatial boundaries: 265 barrios/16 comunas (Medellin, from GeoMedellin) and 189 barrios/5 localidades (Barranquilla, from Secretaria Distrital de Planeacion). Airbnb listings themselves are pulled via an Apify scraper (method, not a static committed dump) rather than stored point-in-time snapshots. README gives no row counts. Repo created/updated 13 Sep 2026 (one day before this scan) — very new, single contributor, unclear maturity.
candidates.why_useful: First concrete LatAm-city STR + regulation/displacement-adjacent dataset found for this theme: ties Colombian Airbnb growth to DANE census and municipal socioeconomic-strata (estrato) data for two cities not in our current Inside Airbnb panel, relevant to gap #12 (regulation/registration context) and gap #7 (regional supply/housing crossover) even though it is not a pure ADR/occupancy series.
candidates.time_coverage: DANE census baseline 2018; estrato layer maintained through 2025; Airbnb pull is live/current via Apify, not vintaged
candidates.size_hint: Several CSVs + one geojson, city-block/barrio granularity (265 + 189 areal units); no listing-level row count given

candidates.name: Airbnb-Rio-de-Janeiro
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed final_data.csv and first_900_rows.csv of Rio de Janeiro Airbnb listings (price-prediction ML project with a Streamlit deploy app). Rio is not in our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel. This is representative of a pattern: gh search returned roughly 25 near-identical 'Airbnb Rio de Janeiro' repos (Joaogabs1346, fredericmenezes, zaninth, mfre1re, matheusbarroso, MaioranoB, EricoCoutoJr, laraaraujoo, brunobarella, jhonatanpaz95, silvaelaine, IsmaelMiranda11, rafael-silva-ifood, Lucasllops, miranda-amanda, matheusbusch, Edu-Paiva, RStremel, Cpizzle1, Igor-Mello, franklin390, PabloHenrique78, lucashcp, ValberJose, eduardocorrearaujo, fabio-hen x2, joaovictordecastroa), almost all appearing to be a Brazilian data-science-bootcamp assignment reusing the same static Rio listings snapshot (likely a single Kaggle/Inside-Airbnb-derived pull, exact vintage unconfirmed) with 1-3 stars each and no unique data beyond the shared base file.
candidates.why_useful: Rio de Janeiro is absent from our held Inside Airbnb panel, so a static listings snapshot is technically new-city coverage, but this looks like the same one-time educational dataset forked/re-scaffolded dozens of times with no point-in-time discipline, no vintage metadata, and likely a single stale pull date — low standalone value versus pulling a fresh Inside Airbnb Rio dump directly if Inside Airbnb covers Rio.
candidates.time_coverage: unknown single vintage, likely 2020-2022 era Kaggle-style pull
candidates.license: MIT (this repo); most of the ~25 near-duplicates have no license declared
candidates.last_activity: 2025-06-11 to 2025-10-03 across the cluster (most recently touched forks/reruns)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Not literally duplicate (Rio is not in our 13-city panel) but functionally near-duplicate across ~25 forks of the same base file

notes: Yield was thin for this theme. gh search repos hit a 403 rate limit mid-run (shared 30/min pool across concurrent scouts) and several later queries (Cancun, Buenos Aires, Sao Paulo, Santiago/Lima, DATATUR/INEGI, Embratur/IBGE, LatAm STR-ordinance-in-Spanish) returned zero results even after retry — GitHub's search-repos endpoint does not surface government tourism-statistics portals or regulation trackers by these keyword combinations, and no committed Sao Paulo/Buenos Aires/Santiago/Lima/Cancun Airbnb dataset repo of any size was found. WebSearch was unavailable for this scout (session-wide 200/200 budget already exhausted by other concurrent scouts before my queries ran), so no web fallback was possible when gh search came up empty — a same-theme scout with WebSearch budget remaining should retry 'site:github.com airbnb bogota/medellin/santiago/lima dataset' and 'DATATUR INEGI turismo github' directly. Suggest a future pass try gh search with topic filters (--topic=short-term-rental, --topic=airbnb) and Spanish/Portuguese terms (alojamiento turistico, aluguel de temporada, regulacion airbnb colombia) which I did not get to before exhausting the recommended call budget. The Rio de Janeiro cluster (~25 near-identical repos) suggests a shared university/bootcamp dataset worth identifying by its original source (possibly a Kaggle 'Airbnb Rio' dataset) rather than cataloguing each fork.
